shortDescription: Manage an approved chaincode on a Hyperledger Fabric channel

options.name: api_authtype
options.description: C(basic) - Authenticate to the Fabric operations console using basic authentication. You must provide both a valid API key using I(api_key) and API secret using I(api_secret).

options.name: api_endpoint
options.description: The URL for the Fabric operations console.

options.name: api_key
options.description: The API key for the Fabric operations console.

options.name: api_secret
options.description: The API secret for the Fabric operations console. Only required when I(api_authtype) is C(basic).

options.name: api_timeout
options.description: The timeout, in seconds, to use when interacting with the Fabric operations console.

options.name: channel
options.description: The name of the channel.

options.name: collections_config
options.description: The path to the collections configuration file for the chaincode definition.

options.name: endorsement_plugin
options.description: The endorsement plugin for this chaincode definition.

options.name: endorsement_policy
options.description: The endorsement policy for this chaincode definition.

options.name: endorsement_policy_ref
options.description: A reference to a channel policy to use as the endorsement policy for this chaincode definition, for example I(/Channel/Application/MyEndorsementPolicy).

options.name: hsm
options.description: The PKCS #11 compliant HSM configuration to use for digital signatures. Only required if the identity specified in I(identity) was enrolled using an HSM.

options.name: identity
options.description: The identity to use when interacting with the peer. You can pass a string, which is the path to the JSON file where the enrolled identity is stored. You can also pass a dict, which must match the result format of one of the M(enrolled_identity_info) or M(enrolled_identity) modules.

options.name: init_required
options.description: True if this chaincode definition requires called the I(Init) method before the I(Invoke) method, false otherwise.

options.name: msp_id
options.description: The MSP ID to use for interacting with the peer.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the chaincode definition.

options.name: orderer_name
options.default: the tls_cert for the orderering service will be found from the channel configuration
options.description: The name of the ordering service node to get the tls-certificate from

options.name: package_id
options.description: The package ID of the chaincode to use for the chaincode definition.

options.name: peer
options.description: The peer to use to manage the approved chaincode definition. You can pass a string, which is the display name of a peer registered with the Fabric operations console. You can also pass a dict, which must match the result format of one of the M(peer_info) or M(peer) modules.

options.name: sequence
options.description: The sequence number of the chaincode definition. If and only if this is set to 0 the next sequence number of chaincode will be calculated. This uses the 'name' as the key to check existing committed chaincodes. If one exists, the highest sequence + 1 is used. Otherwise 1 is used. Makesure to check the return value for the new sequence number

options.name: state
options.description: C(absent) - If a chaincode definition matching the specified name, version and configuration is approved, then an error will be thrown, as it is not possible to unapprove a chaincode definition. C(present) - Asserts that a chaincode definition matching the specified name, version and configuration is approved on the specified channel. If it is not approved, then the chaincode definition with the specified name, version and configuration will be approved on the specified channel.

options.name: validation_plugin
options.description: The validation plugin for this chaincode definition.

options.name: version
options.description: The version of the chaincode definition.
